newsitem.title: TOGO: Zaire summit calls for talks, then ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: Zaire summit calls for talks, then ceasefire.

text.p: An African summit on the crisis in Zaire on Wednesday called for immediate negotiations leading to a ceasefire between President Mobutu Sese Seko's government and rebels.

In a final declaration, the presidents "called for immediate negotiations between the government of Zaire and the Democratic Alliance for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL), leading to a ceasefire and complete cessation of hostilites...."
Rebel leader Laurent Kabila's senior representative at the two-day summit had already announced that the first talks between the warring parties would be held in the next few days.

The summit statement said the talks and ceasefire should lead to implementation of a five-point peace plan by Mohamed Sahnoun, the special U.N. and Organisation of African Unity representative for the Zaire crisis.
Analysts noted that the imminent talks will be held before a ceasefire is in place. This has long been the rebel position.
